I will keep my plan simple and steady. In Quzhou County, I would stick with the wheat-maize rotation on the same land, because that fits our climate, water conditions, machinery, and what I know how to manage well. At my age, I would not spread myself across too many crops. Winter wheat gives me a stable first harvest, and summer maize follows it well and makes full use of the field for the whole year. I would use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want reliable emergence, stronger disease resistance, and better yield without making management too complicated. I would use moderate fertilizer rather than pushing too hard, because grain prices can move around and I care about steady profit more than chasing the very highest yield. I would plough before wheat to prepare a solid seedbed, then use rotary tillage after wheat harvest for quick maize planting. I would irrigate wheat more times than maize, because wheat here depends more on timely water at key stages. I would spray only as needed but still plan for basic weed, disease, and insect control so I do not lose yield from preventable problems. This is the kind of plan I would trust myself to carry through from planting to harvest.
